subject: english
question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

There have been / three breaks-in / in our society / this month.
solution:
The erroneous part is **"three breaks-in"**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In the given sentence, "breaks-in" is incorrect instead of this we need to use "break-ins"
 
• "Break-in" is a noun that means "an illegal forced entry of a building or vehicle, typically to steal something."
 
• The plural form of "break-in" means "break-ins" as we need to use a plural noun since "three" is used which is a plural quantifier.

**Hence, the correct sentence is-** *There have been three **break-ins** in our society this month.*
